summary: cdeops ships obfuscated Function-constructor eval executed on require()
details: The CJS entry points src/index.js, src/client.js, and src/server.js each run an IIFE at module load that uses a custom shuffle cipher (`spin`/`peel`) to reconstruct the string "constructor", retrieves the Function constructor via that decoded property name, and invokes it on a ~15KB cipher-decoded body — executing hidden code whenever a Node.js consumer require()s cdeops, cdeops/client, or cdeops/server. The package otherwise presents itself as a trivial `module.exports = global.require('cdeops')` passthrough shim and the ESM twin files are indeed one-line re-exports, so the ~15KB opaque executable body is confined to the default CJS resolution path. Custom non-standard string obfuscation of the identifier "constructor", of the `global`/`require`/`module` identifiers, and of the eval'd payload itself is used to defeat static inspection; the obfuscation hides the payload's behavior and its network destinations from reviewers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
